## 1. Setup

```{r setup}
# Core libraries
library(glmnet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(foreach)
library(doParallel)
library(progressr)
library(lhs)

# Load all our custom functions
source("../../R/data_generator.R")
source("../../R/solvers.R")


#' Generator for multivariate t-distributed features using LHS
#'
#' Generates an n x p matrix where each column is a sample from a t-distribution,
#' generated via Latin Hypercube Sampling on the probability scale. This ensures
#' a more uniform coverage of the distribution.
#'
#' @param n integer. The number of samples.
#' @param p integer. The number of features.
#' @param df_X numeric. The degrees of freedom for the t-distribution.
#' @param scale_X numeric. A final scaling factor applied to the generated data.
#' @param ... Catches and ignores other arguments (like Sigma_X).
#'
#' @return An n x p matrix of features.
#'
generate_X_t_LHS <- function(n, p, df_X, scale_X = 1, ...) {
  
  # 1. Generate an n x p hypercube using the lhs package.
  # This creates a matrix where each column is a random permutation of
  # (1, 2, ..., n), scaled to be between 0 and 1.
  hypercube <- randomLHS(n, p)
  
  # 2. Apply the inverse CDF (quantile function) of the t-distribution
  # to each element of the hypercube.
  # The `apply` function is not needed as `qt` is vectorized.
  X_raw <- qt(hypercube, df = df_X)
  
  # 3. Apply the final scaling factor
  X_scaled <- X_raw * scale_X
  
  return(X_scaled)
}

```

## 2. Final Simulation Parameters

```{r final-params}
# --- Best Battlefield Data Generation Parameters ---
BEST_SCALE_X <- 1.0
BEST_DF_X <- 2.5
BEST_THETA_MAGNITUDE <- 5.0
DELTA <- 0.5 # df_eps = 1.5

# --- Fixed Model Parameters ---
P <- 600
S_STAR <- 5
THETA_STAR <- rep(0, P)
THETA_STAR[1:S_STAR] <- BEST_THETA_MAGNITUDE

# --- Final Simulation Grid (KEY CHANGE) ---
N_SEQUENCE_FINAL <- c(seq(300, 1200, by=300),400) # Adjusted sequence slightly
METHODS <- c("RIGHT", 
  "IHT", 
  "Shrinkage", 
  "Huber-Lasso", 
  "Lasso"
)
N_REPS_FINAL <- 300 # Increased to final number of replications

param_grid_final <- expand.grid(
  n = N_SEQUENCE_FINAL,
  method = METHODS,
  rep_id = 1:N_REPS_FINAL
)
```

## 3. Main Simulation Loop (Parallel)

```{r main-loop-final, cache=TRUE}
# --- Setup Parallel Backend ---
num_cores <- max(1, detectCores() - 1)
registerDoParallel(cores = num_cores)
cat(sprintf("Running FINAL simulation on %d cores.\n", num_cores))

# --- Run the loop with a progress bar ---
execution_time <- system.time({
  with_progress({
    p_bar <- progressor(steps = nrow(param_grid_final))
    
    results_list <- foreach(
      i = 1:nrow(param_grid_final),
      .combine = 'rbind',
      .packages = c("dplyr", "glmnet","lhs")
    ) %dopar% {
      
      p_bar()
      
      # --- Setup for each task ---
      source("../../R/data_generator.R")
      source("../../R/solvers.R")
      
      params <- param_grid_final[i, ]
      n <- params$n
      method <- as.character(params$method)
      rep_id <- params$rep_id
      
      set.seed(i)
      
      # Generate full dataset
      sim_data <- generate_linear_data(
        n = n, p = P, theta_star = THETA_STAR,
        generator_X = generate_X_t_LHS,
        generator_epsilon = generate_epsilon_t,
        df_X = BEST_DF_X, Sigma_X = diag(P),
        scale_X = BEST_SCALE_X, df_eps = 1 + DELTA
      )
      X_full <- sim_data$X
      y_full <- sim_data$y
      
      # --- UNIFIED 80/20 Split for ALL tuning procedures ---
      train_size <- floor(0.8 * n)
      train_idx <- sample(1:n, size = train_size)
      X_train <- X_full[train_idx, ]; y_train <- y_full[train_idx]
      X_val <- X_full[-train_idx, ]; y_val <- y_full[-train_idx]
      
      # --- Run Solver based on Method (KEY CHANGE) ---
      theta_hat <- switch(
        method,
        "RIGHT" = {
          # Use the winning fixed parameters
          s <- 10; c_K <- 1.0; eta <- 0.01; T_max <- 400
          K <- max(1, round(c_K * log(P * log(n / log(P)))))
          solver_right(X_full, y_full, s, eta, T_max, K, grad_func_samplewise = grad_linear_regression_samplewise)
        },
        "IHT" = {
          s <- 2 * S_STAR; eta <- 0.001; T_max <- 600
          solver_iht(X_full, y_full, s, eta, T_max, grad_func = grad_linear_regression)
        },
        "Lasso" = {
          cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, standardize = FALSE, intercept = FALSE)
          lambda_best <- cv_fit$lambda.min
          final_fit <- glmnet(X_full, y_full, lambda = lambda_best, standardize = FALSE, intercept = FALSE)
          as.vector(final_fit$beta)
        },
        "Shrinkage" = {
          tau_x_fixed <- quantile(abs(X_train), 0.95)
          tau_y_fixed <- quantile(abs(y_train), 0.95)
          X_train_shrunk <- truncate_operator(X_train, tau_x_fixed)
          y_train_shrunk <- truncate_operator(y_train, tau_y_fixed)
          cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(X_train_shrunk, y_train_shrunk, standardize = FALSE, intercept = FALSE)
          lambda_best <- cv_fit$lambda.min
          solver_shrinkage_method(X_full, y_full, tau_x_fixed, tau_y_fixed, lambda_best)
        },
        "Huber-Lasso" = {
          cv_lasso_init <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, standardize = FALSE, intercept = FALSE)
          beta_init_lasso <- as.vector(coef(cv_lasso_init, s = "lambda.min"))[-1]
          residuals_init <- y_train - X_train %*% beta_init_lasso
          tau_fixed <- quantile(abs(residuals_init), 0.95)
          lambda_grid <- 10^seq(-3, 0, length.out = 10)
          best_mse <- Inf
          lambda_best <- NA
          for (lambda_val in lambda_grid) {
            theta_tuned <- solver_huber_lasso(X_train, y_train, lambda_val, tau_fixed, T_max = 250)
            y_pred_val <- X_val %*% theta_tuned
            mse_val <- mean((y_val - y_pred_val)^2)
            if (mse_val < best_mse) {
              best_mse <- mse_val
              lambda_best <- lambda_val
            }
          }
          solver_huber_lasso(X_full, y_full, lambda_best, tau_fixed, T_max = 500)
        }
      )
      
      # --- Calculate and return results ---
      l2_error <- sqrt(sum((theta_hat - THETA_STAR)^2))
      data.frame(n = n, method = method, rep_id = rep_id, l2_error = l2_error)
    }
  })
})

# --- Stop the parallel cluster ---
stopImplicitCluster()
#cat("重复次数", N_REPS_FINAL, " 花费时间")
#print(execution_time)
```

## 4. Analysis and Visualization

```{r analysis-final}
# The result from foreach is already a combined data frame
local_results_df <- results_list

# Aggregate results
summary_local <- local_results_df %>%
  group_by(n, method) %>%
  summarise(mean_l2_error = mean(l2_error, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

print(summary_local)

output_dir <- "../../results/02_Second_simulation_comparison_linear_model"

# Create the directory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# --- Save the final summary object ---
saveRDS(summary_local, file.path(output_dir, "summary_linear_comparison.rds"))

# Also save the raw, unreplicated results if needed
 saveRDS(local_results_df, file.path(output_dir, "raw_results_linear_comparison.rds"))

```

```{r}
#Change Huber-LASSO into Adaptive Huber
summary_local <- summary_local %>%
  mutate(
    method = recode(method, "Huber-Lasso" = "Adaptive Huber")
  )
# Create a version of the data for plotting (without IHT)
plot_data <- summary_local %>%
  filter(method != "IHT") %>%
  mutate(log_n = log(n), log_error = log(mean_l2_error))

# Reorder factor levels for a clean legend, including IHT
# This ensures IHT appears in the legend in the desired order.
all_methods_levels <- c("RIGHT", "Adaptive Huber", "Shrinkage", "Lasso", "IHT")
summary_local$method <- factor(summary_local$method, levels = all_methods_levels)
plot_data$method <- factor(plot_data$method, levels = all_methods_levels)

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Define a color palette for consistent plotting
selected_palette <- c(
  "RIGHT"          = "#332288", # Indigo
  "Adaptive Huber" = "#3B82A1",  # Cyan
  "Shrinkage"      = "#44AA99", # Teal
  "Lasso"          = "#CAB54B" ,# Sand
  "IHT"            = "#CC6677"  # Rose
)


# --- 1. 修改后的绘图代码 ---
linear_comparison_final <- ggplot(
  data = summary_local, 
  aes(x = log(n), y = log(mean_l2_error), color = method, group = method, shape = method)
) +
  # --- 调整线和点的大小 ---
  # Use lines and points to represent the trend for each method
  # linewidth controls line thickness, size controls point size
  geom_line(data = plot_data, linewidth = 1) + 
  geom_point(data = plot_data, size = 2.9) +     
  
  labs(
    x = "Log(Sample Size, n)",
    y = "Log(Mean L2 Error)"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Method", 
    values = selected_palette,
    drop = FALSE 
  ) +
  

  scale_shape_manual(
    name = "Method", 
    values = c("RIGHT" = 16, "Adaptive Huber" = 17, "Shrinkage" = 15, "Lasso" = 12, "IHT" = 4),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  
 
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) + 
  theme(
    
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18), 
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16), 
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),  
    
   
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )


print(linear_comparison_final)


# --- Save the plot to the results directory ---
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "final_comparison_linear_model.pdf"), 
  linear_comparison_final, 
  height = 4, 
  width = 10
)

ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "final_comparison_linear_model.pdf"), 
  linear_comparison_final, 
  height = 4, 
  width = 10, 
  dpi = 300
)
```
